Jaguar Land Rover to cut 4,000 UK jobs, aiming to save £1.7bn

Jaguar Land Rover, owned by Tata Motors, announced a voluntary redundancy programme that will eliminate about 4,000 salaried and management positions in the United Kingdom. The company said the cuts are needed to save roughly £1.7 billion over the next two years as it adapts to evolving global market conditions. Officials linked the restructuring to a slump in profits, falling sales and the impact of U.S. tariffs, noting that the United States accounts for 29 % of JLR’s sales. Trade union partners have been informed of the plan. The announcement was reported by multiple Indian business outlets.
